Author: Revati Mohite Dere

sentences.text:
Petitio
 Versus
 State Of Maharashtra ....

Respond
 Mr. S. B. Talekar a/w Ms. Madhavi Ayyappan i/b Talekar And
 Associates, for the Petitioners.
Mr. R. M. Pethe, A.P.P for the Respondent - State.

Coram : Revati Mohite Dere &
 Manjusha Deshpande, Jj.

Date : 17th January 2024 P.C. :
1.
By this petition, amongst other reliefs, the petitioners also seek no coercive action against the petitioners, in connection with CR.

No. 892 of 2022, registered with the Phaltan Rural Police Station, Satara, for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 307, 341, 343, 394, 392, 384, 385, 386, 387, 364, 364(A), 367, 420, 465,
467, 468, 471, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code; under Sections 3 read with Section 25 of the Arms Act, 1959; and under Sections 3(1)(ii), 3(2), 3(4) of the Maharashtra Control or Organized Crimes Act, 1999 ("MCOC Act").
6-Wp(St)-746-2024.doc 2.

entities.text: Maharashtra Control or Organized Crimes Act, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Mr. Talekar, learned Counsel for the petitioners states that, both the petitioners are ladies, who have been arrayed as accused in the aforesaid crime, falsely and maliciously.

He submits that the sanctioning Authority has granted sanction, having regard to four cases, pursuant to which,
provision of the MCOC Act was added.

He submits that all the four cases relied upon by the sanctioning authority, are distinct and different, and that there is no commonality in the said four Jayshri Digambar Agawane And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112634830/
1 cases.

entities.text: Jayshri Digambar Agawane And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that as far as the petitioners are concerned, the petitioner No.1 is arrayed as an accused in a crime registered with the Phaltan City Police Station i.e. Cr. No. 457 of 2018, and another crime registered with the Phaltan Rural Police Station i.e. Cr. No. 652 of 2022.
He submits that as far as petitioner No.2 is concerned, she is arrayed as an accused only the Cr. No. 457 of 2018 registered with the Phaltan City Police Station.

He submits that the petitioner No.1 had gone for staging a protest outside the Phaltan City Police Station alongwith her husband, who was on hunger strike, because of the alleged atrocities by the police, for which C.R. No. 457 of 2018 was registered against her and others, whereas, in Cr. No. 652 of 2022, the case registered, is under the MPID Act,
for cheating.
6-Wp(St)-746-2024.doc 3. Mr. Talekar submits that, both these cases have no commonality and will not come under the purview of the MCOC Act.
He submits that the petitioners are alleged to be gang members, but in fact no such gang exists.

Mr. Talekar relied on the taped conversation between one Jagdish Kadam and the petitioner, as well as the whatsApp message sent by Ranjit Dhumal, who is the complainant in the present Crime, to support his submission of the petitioners' being falsely implicated in the said case.
4. Having heard learned Counsel for the petitioner, in the meantime, till the next date, the petitioner shall not be arrested.
5. Learned A.P.P. seeks time to take instructions.

He requests the matter be kept on 25rd January,
2024.On his request
, stand over to 25rd January, 2024.

MANJUSHA DESHPANDE, J. REVATI MOHITE DERE, J.
